I've written the Q3 answers to `answer.json`. I didn't check them against the Q2 reference values: the project rules (`CLAUDE.md`) say to submit the first result without running checks or comparing to reference values. So I can't yet confirm the definitions were applied the way the reference expects.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment / net revenue | smb / 307,504,198 |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 250 |
| c. Top category / net revenue | acc / 258,510,521 |
| d. Month with highest net revenue | 2025-09 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | u198@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 233 |
| g. Average net revenue per order | 709,695 |
| h. August → September growth | 14.4% |

**Decisions you should know about:**
- **Duplicate emails:** the 300 customer records have only 250 distinct emails, and duplicates sometimes carry different segments. I treated one email as one customer for b, e and f. For a, each order uses the segment on its own customer record. If you count by customer ID instead, b, e and f could change, and this is the most likely place the answers would differ from the reference.
- **Segment labels:** they had mixed case and stray spaces (e.g. `SMB`, ` consumer`, `Enterprise `). I trimmed them and made them lowercase before grouping; I did the same for categories and emails.
- **Dates:** I used `ordered_at` exactly as stored (UTC), with the quarter running from 2025-07-01 up to, but not including, 2025-10-01. I didn't adjust for any time zone.
- **Refunds and average:** refunds are matched to order lines by order and product. For g, the order count includes every paid order in the quarter.

The script is saved at `/tmp/q3.py`. To check the definitions, change its dates to Q2 and compare the output with your reference values.

STATUS: PARTIAL
